stagger(*iterables, fillvalue=None, uneven_fillvalue=None, fillvalue_on_partial=False)
    "Return an iterator that returns elements from the first iterable until
    it is exhausted, then fills from the second iterable, until it is
    exhausted, and so on.  If the iterables are of different lengths,
    the remaining elements from the shorter iterables are filled with the
    fillvalue.  If uneven_fillvalue is specified, the fillvalue for the
    last iterable is set to this value.
    
    :param iterables: the iterables to stagger
    :type iterables: iterable
    :param fillvalue: the value to fill with when the iterables are of
        different lengths
    :type fillvalue: any
    :param uneven_fillvalue: the value to fill with for the last iterable
        when iterables are of different lengths
    :type uneven_fillvalue: any
    :param fillvalue_on_partial: if True, fill the remaining space in the
        last iterable with the fillvalue
    :type fillvalue_on_partial: bool
    :rtype: iterator
    
    Examples:
    >>> list(stagger([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6, 7]))  # doctest: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE
    [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
    >>> list(stagger([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6, 7], fillvalue_on_partial=True))  # doctest: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE
    [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    >>> list(stagger([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], uneven_fillvalue=7))  # doctest: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE
    [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
